findings.rationale: GU is the only client that stands out in the update screens. Its update norms are high for its size (size-adjusted median_norm_ratio flagged at z=+4.3), and its mean cosine to the median update is the lowest in the federation (0.166, against a typical 0.4-0.7). Per-round values (c11) are erratic: cosines are near 0.78 average in rounds 1-7 but about -0.13 average in rounds 8-20, while norms rise to about 1.26x the median. Signs flip from round to round, which fits large random noise in the uploads rather than a consistent sign-flip. Local AUC is normal (0.83), so accuracy barely moves, as expected for explanation jitter. Local calibration also shows a mild ECE outlier (z=+3.2). Evidence is moderate: the per-round values are noisy at n=708, and the budget was exhausted before I could confirm the onset round. Other drift and subgroup outliers (AL, PR, IL, NV, VI, VA, MA, AR) looked like noise: their shifts were not sustained, and their subgroup values were inconsistent across queries.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then ran narrower follow-ups on the suspicious clients. Most of the outliers did not hold up: their drift shifts were not sustained, and their subgroup values changed between queries, which points to noise from small samples. The one client with a consistent multi-signal anomaly is GU (small, n=708). Its updates are oversized for its size, have the lowest cosine to the median update, and turn erratic from about round 8, while its local AUC stays normal. I classed this as explanation_instability with moderate confidence (0.5). The budget is now fully spent (0 left), so the onset round and the GU fault type could not be confirmed further. I did not report any other client.
